searches.note: Twenty two searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; six left unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: cantina5terre.com twice (the Sciacchetrà and Riserva sheets, the grappa), terrebianche.com once (the history), cantinelunae.com once (Etichetta Grigia), lescretes.it once (the family) and cavemontblanc.com once (the still wine's and Cuvée du Prince's sheets). Five blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show (the co-operative's founding, the Rossese DOC, Bricco Arcagna, Lunae's founding and making, Les Crêtes' history and Cuvée Bois, the Chamber of Commerce). Four went to the decrees and their copies (Cinque Terre, Rossese di Dolceacqua, Colli di Luni, Valle d'Aosta and Pornassio), and the rest to the press, the regional pages and the merchants. The Valle d'Aosta DOC search served Les Crêtes and the Cave alike and is counted with the Cave. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages and sheets for their own dates and methods and to the decrees and their copies, then to the regional pages, the press and the merchants, with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves.

Where the sources corrected the record (the Sciacchetrà's drying and its small oak, the Riserva's three years, Bricco Arcagna's steel and year in barrel, Arcagna's altitude, the nomeranze, the family of Les Crêtes from over the Alps rather than France, the trap that made every Chardonnay of the valley a DOC wine, the Cave's association of 1971) the record was set right with its source; where a detail rested on no source the refuter read (the hand destemming, the repair of the terraces, Mount Aurin, organic farming, Liguria's and the Valle d'Aosta's wants of a DOCG and an IGT, the move of 1989, the harvest date set by growers' bodies, Petite Arvine's grapefruit and rhubarb) it was cut or set as the sources give it.
Prices on the houses' shops and the merchants' pages, a guide's glasses and a critic's points, members, hectares, vine ages and bottles a year were read and not used.

tested: Founded 1973: the LEI register gives the co-operative's creation on 30 March 1973 under its legal name, which lists the five villages and allows Cantina 5 Terre or Cantina Cinque Terre in short; the search summary of the Ministry's disciplinare page also gives 1973 for the cellar and co-operative. Confirmed.
The DOC of 1973 for the dry white and Sciacchetrà: the text of 1973 as copied by Disciplinare.it and Assovini gives approval by a decree of 29 May 1973, published in August 1973. Confirmed.

Release a year after the harvest and the Riserva not before the third year: the AIS copy and Federvini's notice of the amendment of 2021 move the day from 1 November to 1 October of the year after the harvest, and of the third year after it for the Riserva. Confirmed and set in the making.

The grapes and the drying: the house's sheets give Bosco by far the larger part with Albarola and Vermentino, dried naturally on racks for about two months, fermented on the skins and aged in small oak, the Riserva at least three years. The record's drying out of the sun for seventy days (Slow Food) and its hand destemming were replaced or cut; a producer of the DOC (Cinque Terre Wine House's sheet) has racks out of the sun until November, which the record does not need.

Sciac-trà the rosé of Ormeasco di Pornassio, from Dolcetto: Italian Wine Central and the AIS copy of the Pornassio rules give a Sciac-trà type of at least 95 per cent Ormeasco, the local name for Dolcetto, briefly macerated. Confirmed.

UNESCO 1997, the monorails and the fifty years of the DOC: UNESCO's page stands for the inscription; the monorails are the record's own and widely told, kept; the house's fiftieth anniversary bottling of the Cinque Terre DOC of 2022 agrees with 1973.

The house rules: no living person named, no price (the shop's prices met and not used), no member or bottle count, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, four options of a kind (four sweetening methods; four events on the coast), the explanations teach.

open: The drying: the house says naturally on racks for about two months, a producer's sheet racks out of the sun until November, and the national park's page by the author's report bunches dried in the sun; the record follows the house and makes no claim of sun or shade.
Bosco's least share in the Sciacchetrà was not read in the decree; the Cinque Terre white's 40 per cent in one guide is not carried over.

tested: Founded 1870 by the family's account, the white soil and the first Rossese: the house's English and Italian pages, read through search, give the planting of the first Rossese on a patch of white soil in 1870 by an ancestor; kept as the house's claim. The ancestor has no dates and is described, not named.

The DOC of 1972, the first of Liguria: the AIS copy of the disciplinare gives approval by a decree of 28 January 1972, published in May 1972; AIS Liguria and Lavinium call it the first DOC approved in Liguria; the house gives the same. Two independent sources beside the house: the lint's note of a first is answered, and the classification, story and question stand.
The family among the DOC's founders: the house's Italian page names a member of an earlier generation, now dead, as one of the founders in 1972. Kept as the house tells it.

Bricco Arcagna's making: Galli Enoteca's sheet gives destemmed grapes on native yeasts and barrels of 225 litres; DiWineTaste twelve months in barrique; a listing quoting the house fermentation in steel and almost a year in used barriques; Vinopoly casks of 225 and 500 litres. Set as fermented in steel and about a year in oak barrels, barriques among them.

The sites: AIS Lombardia gives Arcagna at 320 to 420 metres against the house's 380 to 450 as merchants quote it; the record now says around 400 metres, the aspect cut. Terrabianca: the house gives white clay and blue marl, a merchant blue clays and blue marls; the record says clay and blue marl.

Nomeranze: AIS Lombardia, Intravino and Galli Enoteca give it as the local word for the additional geographical mentions of the DOC, 33 of them, Arcagna at Dolceacqua and Terrabianca among them; not a word of the house's own, so the story is set right.

The history of the hill: the house's pages give a small Ligurian lookout tower, a Roman family (the Aurinia) holding land in the valley and the Benedictines of Santa Maria at Dolceacqua, from Novalesa in the Italian page. Mount Aurin is not in them; changed.

The house rules: the living members of the family met and not named, the vine ages (over fifty and some over a hundred and twenty years, a figure that grows) and the bottle count met and not used; no price, no score, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, four Ligurian appellations and four years, the explanations teach.

The making: Il Vino Manduria, Enoteca Maggiolini and other listings give about eight hours of cold maceration and about four months on fine lees in steel; Svinando and Leone Blu give up to forty eight hours; AIS Lombardia a cold maceration in the press and a few months on the lees for older vintages. Changed to a short cold maceration; the four months kept.

The Colli di Luni DOC of 1989, by a decree of 14 June 1989: AIS Liguria (instituted in 1989) and Wikiwand (14 June 1989), with the AIS copy the author read. Vermentino at least 90 per cent for the Vermentino: the Ministry's catalogue and AIS Liguria. The province of Massa Carrara: the Ministry's text names Fosdinovo, Aulla and Podenzana. Confirmed.

Etichetta Grigia the founder's first Vermentino: the house's page and its sheet, read through search, say it was the first wine of Vermentino its founder made, more than forty years ago. Confirmed as the house's account.

The house rules: the founder and his son are living and described; the house's awards pages met and not used; no price, no score, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, four methods of cellar work and four origins of a name, the explanations teach.

The turn to wine: the region's page has the family's mill run until 1955, when oil and milled grain came in from outside the valley and the family turned to wine; the author read first vines of 1955 in a second account. Added.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment; the read together agent adds the six to people.json. Of unsettled status and not named: Claudio Rondelli, Filippo's father (reported dead by the author without dates) and Marthe, the Bordeaux born wife of an earlier Rondelli, whom the house's page names; Antoine Charrère, the founder's father, who made the house's first Sabla in 1970 by its account. Long dead and not named for want of dates: the Rondelli ancestor of 1870 and an earlier Rondelli among the DOC's founders, the Charrère forebear of about 1750, and the parish priest of Morgex who urged the association of 1971.
swapNote: No swap proposed and none ruled. All five picks stand: the co-operative of the Cinque Terre with its Sciacchetrà, Terre Bianche with its single hill Rossese, Lunae with its fuller Vermentino, Les Crêtes with the Chardonnay Enocode credits with the house's name, and the Cave with its still white of the sub-zone, the region record naming four of the five houses.
planNotes: cantina-cinque-terre: the note is answered: founded on 30 March 1973 (the LEI register; the Ministry's disciplinare page), the name as it writes it is Agricoltura di Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza e Monterosso, in short Cantina 5 Terre or Cantina Cinque Terre, on its site cantina5terre.com; the label reads Cinque Terre Sciacchetrà DOC, of Bosco with Albarola and Vermentino. The why stands.

terre-bianche: the note is answered: 1870 is the house's own date, told as its account; labels and listings read Rossese di Dolceacqua, the DOC's lawful pair of names being Rossese di Dolceacqua or Dolceacqua, and no source the refuter read calls Bricco Arcagna a Superiore. The why stands.

lunae: the note is answered: 1966 in most accounts (one listing gives 1970); the house writes Cantine Lunae, styled LVNAE, and listings print Lunae Bosoni and Colli di Luni Vermentino Etichetta Nera. The why stands.

les-cretes: the note is answered: 1989 by the region's page and the house; Enocode calls Cuvée Bois the wine that did most for the house's name, first made in 1995, so the pick is kept and Petite Arvine stays among the others. No living member of the family is named. The why's family long rooted in the valley holds, from about 1750.

cave-mont-blanc: the note is answered: the still DOC white, which the house lists among its whites under its own name, Cave Mont Blanc; the house writes Cave Mont Blanc de Morgex et La Salle, a co-operative society. The why's co-operative of 1983 and its 1,200 metres stand.

codexNote: Reported and not edited: the region record is left to the owner, as wave one's codexInTension entries are. The region record's Sciacchetrà sold in small bottles, which the author could not confirm, is borne out by the co-operative's Riserva sheet (half bottles of 375 millilitres); its drying for weeks on racks, its first DOC of 1972 and its Cinque Terre of 1973 agree with the decrees and the house.
